components.name: Web client
responsibilities: React and TypeScript single-page app in frontend/, built with Vite and served by nginx in deployment
Sign-in, registration of the first account and user administration

Flows page: lists top-level task flows (by their current name) and chats, and a task flow's requirements or onboarding interview, requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery children with pending, skipped and linked-from-another-task marks; opens chats, sessions and onboardings in a panel; the Requirements and Onboarding filters list task flows of that origin through the origin filter, and old-shape requirements and onboarding flows from before this change are shown only in the All view

Shows the requirements review flow with its rounds and, when the user continued anyway, the contradictions that remained; shows the review's status, contradiction questions and any reviewer error in the requirements and onboarding sessions, with a retry button for a failed review round
Asks for confirmation in a warning modal window before finalizing with force while the review reports contradictions or has failed

Shows an open task flow as running and highlights it, and each of its children, as waiting for the user and with the unresolved findings marker as GET /workflows reports them, instead of deriving them from the children's sessions; opens the waiting child's questions from the highlight
Old-shape requirements and onboarding flows from before this change and their stages are only listed and opened, with no waiting-for-user highlight and no unresolved findings marker
Opens the next stage from a session's returned IDs: the architecture session, the API design session, or the delivery of a bugfix or documentation change
Repository and branch picker, GitHub connection settings and the Settings page, which includes the requirements reviewer's model
Shows delivery progress, agent questions, review findings and pull request links, and sends the user's answers and decisions

components.name: HTTP API
responsibilities: FastAPI application (app.api.main) exposing the auth, chat, requirements, architecture, API design, onboarding, workflows and GitHub connector routes
Requires a signed-in user on every router except auth and the GitHub webhook endpoint
Validates input, bounds request sizes and maps Temporal and storage failures to 503 and session errors to 404/409/422
Starts, queries, signals and updates Temporal workflows for each session through the session services

Creates the database schemas at startup (including the model settings table) and runs background loops: expired-document cleanup, Pi OAuth credential refresh and recovery of interrupted webhook mentions
At startup, cancels every still-running old-shape OnboardingWorkflow (top-level, without a parent task flow) started before this change; the step is idempotent, so later startups find none

components.name: Auth module
responsibilities: Registers the first account as administrator and lets the administrator create and list accounts (app.auth)
Hashes passwords with salted scrypt and verifies them at sign-in
Issues and checks HS256 JWT session tokens signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET, sent as bearer tokens or the HttpOnly access_token cookie
Rate-limits sign-in and registration attempts per client address

components.name: Session services
responsibilities: Per-flow services (app.requirements, app.architecture, app.api_design, app.onboarding, app.conversations, app.delivery service modules) that turn API calls into Temporal workflow starts, queries, signals and updates

Start a TaskWorkflow, with origin requirements or onboarding, for every new requirements interview and onboarding, for every fork of a requirements, architecture, API design or onboarding interview session (linked to the original task's earlier stages, carrying over the forked interview's review state) and for every fix round on a closed delivery of a task or onboarding

Pass finalize, with or without the force flag, to the requirements or onboarding interview; force is accepted at any point of the review (before it has run, during a running round, or after contradictions or a reviewer error) and writes the document at once
Pass the retry of a failed review round from the requirements or onboarding session to its requirements review; retrying when the last round did not fail answers 409

Read session state, conversation, drafts, the requirements review's status, round, contradictions and any reviewer error, delivery progress and the task flow's ID and next stage's ID (architecture session, API design session, or the delivery of a bugfix or documentation change) from workflow queries for the API responses
Hand authorised pull request mentions to the delivery workflow they belong to, for tasks and onboardings alike

List workflow executions with their repository, branch, task name, task origin, pending/skipped state, linked-task, waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings search attributes and the workflow registry (app.temporal.executions, app.temporal.registry). top_level lists task flows, chats, the old-shape requirements flows and the cancelled old-shape onboarding flows started before this change. parent lists a flow's direct children plus stages linked to it, and an old-shape flow's children as before. The origin filter lists only task flows of that origin. No onboarding ID is returned or accepted as a filter any more

For closed deliveries and task flows, clear the listed unresolved findings marker when a findings acceptance record (app.delivery.acceptances) exists for the closed delivery run, since a closed workflow can no longer update its own search attributes
The workflow_type filter for task flows lists only TaskWorkflow executions, so old-shape RequirementsWorkflow and OnboardingWorkflow executions appear only in the unfiltered (All) listing
Onboarding sessions of old-shape onboardings cancelled on deploy remain readable but accept no further actions (409)

components.name: Orchestration worker
responsibilities: Temporal worker on the main task queue (app.temporal.worker)
Runs LLMRequestWorkflow, TaskWorkflow, RequirementsWorkflow, RequirementsReviewWorkflow, ArchitectureWorkflow, ApiDesignWorkflow, OnboardingWorkflow and DeliveryWorkflow

TaskWorkflow (top-level per task, with an origin of requirements or onboarding): creates its stage children up front: requirements, requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery for a new service or API change; requirements, requirements review and delivery for a bugfix; requirements and delivery for documentation; onboarding interview, requirements review and delivery for an onboarding. It holds each one pending until the stages it depends on have finished, then starts it, and closes skipped stages. It stays running (its Temporal status) for as long as any child is pending or running

TaskWorkflow starts the pending requirements review when the requirements or onboarding interview is finalized (except for documentation, an idle-written session or onboarding, or an architecture-only onboarding, whose review closes as skipped). It starts the next stage only once the review passes or the user continues despite contradictions: the delivery of a bugfix or onboarding, or the architecture of a new service or API change. It starts the API design when the architecture is finalized or skipped, and for documentation it starts the delivery as soon as the requirements are finalized

RequirementsReviewWorkflow (new, one child per task across all its rounds): in each round an LLM checks the session's requirements against each other and against the existing service's requirements the task has not retired; for an onboarding that replaces an existing contract, the drafted requirements are also checked against that contract's requirements. From the second round on, the reviewer is given both the diff of the requirement records since its previous round (added, changed and removed, with their texts) and the contradiction questions with the user's answers. It returns the contradictions to the requirements or onboarding interview, which asks the user one question per contradiction. Once all are answered, the interview hands the updated requirements back for the next round. Rounds are unlimited. It closes as passed when no contradictions remain, or as continued anyway with the remaining contradictions when the user finalizes with force

When a review round's LLM activity still fails after its Temporal retries (provider unavailable or invalid output), the round is marked failed with the reviewer's error and treated like a round with contradictions found (none listed): the session shows the error and the user can either retry the round through a retry action, like retrying a failed turn, which runs the same round again with the same input, or continue with force; nothing later starts on its own

Finalize with force writes the requirements document at once whatever the review's state: a running review round is cancelled, and a review that has not run yet is closed as continued anyway with no contradictions; the remaining contradictions of the last finished round are listed in the document
Requirements and onboarding reviews use the same requirements_review model settings entry

Requirements and onboarding interviews keep the review's status, round and contradictions for their session responses, write the requirements document only after the review passes or is forced, and list the remaining contradictions in it when it was forced. A forked requirements or onboarding interview copies the review state (status, round and contradictions) of the session it was forked from at the fork point, and its new task flow's review continues from that round

An onboarding interview idle for a day is closed like an idle requirements session: its requirements document is written without a review, and its review and delivery children close as skipped, so its task flow closes as cancelled

OnboardingWorkflow is the onboarding interview stage of an onboarding TaskWorkflow: it no longer starts its own delivery but hands its finalized contract to the task flow, whose delivery child verifies, reviews and pushes it (code generation runs under that delivery). Fix rounds on a closed onboarding's pull request and forks of an onboarding interview start a new onboarding TaskWorkflow, as they do for tasks

TaskWorkflow keeps the task's short name: written by an LLM from the intake at start and rewritten from the finalized requirements; a task flow started by a fork or a fix round on a closed delivery copies the original task's name with a '(fork)' or '(fix)' suffix, and a fork's name is still rewritten when its requirements are finalized
TaskWorkflow closes with its delivery child's status (cancelled when the delivery was skipped) once every child, including the earlier stages it links to from a fork or fix round, has closed

Stage workflows keep their own waiting-for-user state (unanswered interviewer or contradiction questions, a failed review round, coding agent questions, open review findings, a skip proposal or a contract decision) and unresolved-findings state as search attributes, cleared when the flow closes so a closed flow is never waiting (FR-110)

Stages report every change of their waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings state to their TaskWorkflow, which aggregates its children's states into its own WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings search attributes

Stage workflows report their hand-off (requirements or onboarding interview finalized or idle-written, review passed or forced, architecture finalized or skip confirmed, API design finalized, pull request merged or closed) to their TaskWorkflow instead of starting the next stage themselves, and on closing signal every task flow they are linked into
Activities for LLM interviewer turns and drafting, requirements review rounds, writing the requirements, architecture and OpenAPI documents, and naming task flows
Activities for repository checkout and contract reading, pushing deliveries, documentation and onboardings, and opening or updating pull requests with LLM-written text
Classifies mentions of the GitHub App, replies to them and answers clarifications
DeliveryWorkflow runs code generation, implementation, test generation, verification with diagnosis and repair rounds, code review rounds and the push as child workflows on the other task queues

Requirements executions started before this change keep running in their old shape (stages under a RequirementsWorkflow) and are not migrated; old-shape top-level OnboardingWorkflows are cancelled on deploy, together with their delivery and code generation children, and have to be started again

components.name: Codegen worker
responsibilities: Temporal worker on the codegen task queue running CodegenWorkflow (app.codegen.worker)
Runs openapi-generator to turn the finalized OpenAPI document into server code for the chosen language
Writes the generated code to GENERATED_CODE_DIR for the next stages

components.name: Sandbox worker
responsibilities: One host process with a Temporal worker per sandboxed stage and its own task queue: implementation, test generation, verification, diagnosis, code review and documentation, one activity at a time each (app.agent_workflows.worker)
Builds agent images and starts, monitors and removes coding agent containers through a Docker daemon (app.docker_agents)
Passes the workspace, LLM settings and provider credentials into containers and re-logs their output
Keeps the workspace of an agent that paused with questions and resumes it with the user's answers
Builds the service from its root Dockerfile and runs the contract test suites against it (Python and Java test-suite images) for verification and baseline checks

components.name: Coding agent containers
responsibilities: Isolated Docker containers, one per agent run, built from app/agent_workflows/Dockerfile with the role's agent.py
Implementation, test generation, diagnosis, code review and documentation agents that read and write only their mounted workspace
Call the LLM through the LangChain, Pi or Claude adapter with the stage's model settings
Pause with questions for the user by saving their state in the workspace
Have no access to Temporal, PostgreSQL or the Docker daemon

components.name: LLM adapters
responsibilities: Build the chat model for a workflow from its model settings (app.llm.factory): OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini through LangChain, the Pi coding agent CLI, or Claude through the Claude Agent SDK
Run the LangGraph tool-calling agent with the session tools (requirements, architecture, API design, repository, documents and questions tools in app.tools)
Normalize the questions the LLM asks the user
Optionally trace LLM calls to Langfuse

components.name: GitHub connector
responsibilities: Stores the shared GitHub App connection with its private key and webhook secret encrypted with Fernet (app.github.storage)
Calls the GitHub REST API as the app: installation tokens, repositories, branches, manifest conversion, webhook configuration, pull requests and comments (app.github.client)
Checks out and pushes branches with git using installation tokens (app.github.checkout)
Verifies webhook signatures, deduplicates deliveries and comments, and admits only authorised mentions on the app's pull requests (app.github.webhooks)

components.name: Document storage
responsibilities: Stores uploaded attachments and generated documents with their metadata in PostgreSQL and their originals on disk under DOCUMENT_STORAGE_DIR (app.documents)
Parses uploads into searchable session passages
Deletes expired documents

components.name: Model settings
responsibilities: Internal storage of the adapter, model and thinking level chosen for each LLM workflow type (app.settings), now including a requirements_review entry for the requirements reviewer of tasks and onboardings alike, separate from the code review entry
Knows the models and thinking levels each provider offers
Provides the settings the workers and agent containers use for their LLM calls

components.name: PostgreSQL
responsibilities: Stores application data in the app schema: users, GitHub connection, pull requests, webhook deliveries and comments, mention admissions, delivery mentions, onboarding sessions, documents and passages, workflow settings and the workflow registry
Stores Temporal's persistence and visibility databases in deployment

components.name: Temporal server
responsibilities: Persists workflow state and dispatches workflow and activity tasks to the workers by task queue
Keeps the Repository and Branch search attributes used to list executions; OnboardingId is no longer set on new executions or returned

Keeps the FlowState (pending or skipped, overriding the Temporal status in listings), TaskName and LinkedTaskFlows (keyword list of task flows a stage is linked into by a fork or fix round) search attributes, upserted by the workflows
Keeps the new TaskOrigin keyword search attribute (requirements or onboarding), set when a TaskWorkflow starts, which the origin filter queries
Keeps the WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings boolean search attributes, upserted by stages and task flows, so listings carry the backend-computed highlight and marker

components.name: GitHub
responsibilities: External service: the GitHub REST API at api.github.com and git hosting of the repositories the shared GitHub App installation can access
Issues installation tokens, converts app manifests and holds the app's webhook configuration, pull requests and comments
Delivers signed webhook events for pull request conversation and inline review comments

components.name: LLM provider
responsibilities: External service: the model endpoints chosen in the model settings (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Google Gemini, the providers behind the Pi CLI, or Anthropic's Claude)
Answers the chat, interviewer, drafting, requirements review, code review, pull request text, mention classification and coding agent model calls

components.name: Langfuse
responsibilities: External, optional tracing service that receives traces of LLM calls, of the main and codegen queues' activity executions and of sandboxed stage operations
Used only when LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL are set and LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED is not false

data_flows.description: JSON (and multipart for chat attachments) over HTTP under /api through the frontend's proxy, with the access_token cookie; the client polls sessions and workflow lists for progress.
In-process calls: credentials for registration and sign-in, and the bearer token or cookie of every protected request to resolve the signed-in user.
Users with their scrypt password hashes and creation times, read and written with psycopg.
In-process calls with validated session actions: messages, answers, forks, finalize, skip, checkout, contract decisions, agent answers, findings decisions, stage retries and workflow list filters.

Temporal client gRPC calls: start TaskWorkflows (with TaskOrigin) and chats with search attributes, send signals and updates to the task flow and its stages (including finalize with force and the retry of a failed review round), run queries for session and review state, and list executions by visibility queries over ParentWorkflowId, LinkedTaskFlows, FlowState, TaskOrigin and the other search attributes.
Workflow registry entries, onboarding sessions and delivery mentions, read and written with psycopg.
In-process calls: connect, check and remove the app, list repositories and branches, and hand over raw webhook deliveries with their signature for verification and mention admission.
The connection with its Fernet-encrypted private key and webhook secret, the app's pull requests, handled webhook deliveries and comments, and mention admissions.
In-process calls: chat attachments to store, and document IDs to stream back as downloads.
Document metadata and parsed session passages; the originals are written to files on disk.
The workflow_settings row with the model settings of every LLM workflow type.

Workflow and activity tasks of the main task queue over gRPC. The worker returns results, starts TaskWorkflow stage children (pending ones wait for a start signal from their task flow) and starts child workflows on the codegen and sandboxed stage queues. Stage workflows signal their task flow at each hand-off and on every change of their waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings state, and, when they close, every task flow in their LinkedTaskFlows. In each review round the requirements or onboarding interview signals the review with the current requirements, the diff since the previous round and the contradiction questions with the user's answers, and the review signals back the contradictions found. The task flow signals pending stages to start or close as skipped, and workflows upsert their search attributes.
CodegenWorkflow tasks with the OpenAPI document and language over gRPC; the result names the generated code directory.

Implementation, test generation, verification, diagnosis, review and documentation workflow tasks over gRPC, each on its own task queue; results carry workspaces, verdicts, findings or agent questions.

In-process calls with the conversation, session tools and the workflow's model settings for interviewer turns, drafting, chat answers, task flow names, pull request text and mention classification and replies.
In-process calls to check out the session's branch and read its contract, push deliveries and onboardings to new branches, open or update pull requests and post mention replies.
Parses uploads into passages and writes generated requirements, architecture and OpenAPI documents.
Reads the model settings of the workflow type an LLM activity runs for.

Docker CLI calls to a dedicated Docker daemon: builds the agent image, copies in the workspace (contract, generated code, tests, review findings, answers) and the stage's model settings file, passes provider credentials as environment variables, and copies the workspace and agent state back out.
Reads each stage's model settings to pass into its agent container.
In-process calls inside the container: the agent runs the adapter code copied into its image with the stage's model settings file.
Admitted pull request mentions handed to the delivery workflow they belong to (of a task or an onboarding) as Temporal signals or updates, delivered through the Temporal server.
Generated server code passed as files under GENERATED_CODE_DIR on the shared /data volume, which the implementation stage copies into its workspace.

REST calls over HTTPS through httpx, authenticated with RS256 app JWTs and installation tokens (installations, repositories, branches, manifest conversion, webhook configuration, pull requests and comments), and git clone and push over HTTPS with installation tokens.
Webhook deliveries (issue_comment and pull_request_review_comment events) POSTed to /connectors/github/events with the X-Hub-Signature-256, X-GitHub-Event and X-GitHub-Delivery headers.

Model calls over HTTPS with the conversation, tools and the workflow's model and thinking level, through LangChain clients, the Pi CLI or the Claude Agent SDK, from the workers and from inside agent containers with the forwarded credentials.
Traces of LLM calls (LangChain callback handler, Claude plugin hook) exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys, with secrets redacted and content capture optional.
Spans of sandboxed stage operations (agent runs, diagnosis, review) over HTTPS; the trace context and Langfuse settings are passed into agent containers as environment variables.

Spans of the main queue's activity executions (interviewer turns, drafting, document writing, mention handling), tagged with the Temporal workflow, run, activity ID and attempt by the trace_activity decorator (app.temporal.tracing), exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys when tracing is enabled; replayed workflow code is never traced.

Spans of the generate-server-code activity (CodegenWorkflow), tagged with the Temporal workflow, run, activity ID and attempt by the trace_activity decorator (app.temporal.tracing), exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys when tracing is enabled.

technology_choices.choice: Python 3.12 with FastAPI, served by uvicorn
technology_choices.rationale: Required by TR-1; async request handling fits the Temporal and httpx clients.

technology_choices.choice: Temporal (temporalio Python SDK, server 1.31) with separate task queues for the main, codegen and each sandboxed stage worker
technology_choices.rationale: Long-running sessions that wait on the user, retries of single stages and child workflows per stage; separate queues keep each stage to one container at a time.

technology_choices.choice: PostgreSQL 16 through psycopg 3 for application data and Temporal persistence; uploaded originals and generated code on a disk volume
technology_choices.rationale: Required by TR-1; one database server serves both the app and Temporal.

technology_choices.choice: React 19 with TypeScript, built with Vite, react-markdown for rendered documents

LangChain/LangGraph tool-calling agents over OpenAI-compatible endpoints or Google Gemini, plus the Pi coding agent CLI and the Claude Agent SDK as alternative adapters, chosen per workflow type in the model settings
technology_choices.rationale: Lets each workflow use a different provider and model without code changes.

technology_choices.choice: Docker containers started through a separate Docker-in-Docker daemon (docker:dind under the Sysbox runtime) whose socket only the sandbox worker mounts, on its own network without private addresses
technology_choices.rationale: TR-2: agents must not reach Temporal, the database or Docker.

technology_choices.choice: openapi-generator, run as a subprocess by the codegen worker
technology_choices.rationale: Produces server scaffolding from the finalized OpenAPI document before the coding agents fill it in.

technology_choices.choice: One shared GitHub App: REST API through httpx with RS256 app JWTs and installation tokens, git CLI for checkout and push, signed webhooks (HMAC-SHA256) for pull request comment mentions
technology_choices.rationale: Lets the instance act on repositories without user tokens and receive mentions.

technology_choices.choice: HS256 JWTs via PyJWT, scrypt password hashes from hashlib, Fernet (cryptography) encryption of the GitHub App key and webhook secret
Optional Langfuse tracing of LLM calls and stage operations, also from inside agent containers
technology_choices.rationale: Active only when the Langfuse keys and base URL are set (LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED defaults to true but can turn it off); secrets are redacted from traces.

technology_choices.choice: Docker Compose (Coolify): frontend with nginx, api, worker, codegen-worker, sandbox-worker, sandbox daemon, PostgreSQL, Temporal and Temporal UI; the root Dockerfile builds the API alone with its own PostgreSQL on port 8080 as a non-root user
technology_choices.rationale: TR-3: the root image is a self-contained service for contract tests; deployments use backend/Dockerfile.

technology_choices.choice: A TaskWorkflow per task or onboarding on the main queue starts every stage as its Temporal child at once and carries a TaskOrigin search attribute. A stage not yet allowed to work waits for a start signal and carries FlowState=pending, and a stage that will never run closes with FlowState=skipped. Links of forked or fix-round task flows to earlier stages are the LinkedTaskFlows keyword-list search attribute on those stages. The OnboardingId attribute is dropped.
technology_choices.rationale: FR-125 to FR-140, FR-159, FR-164 and FR-166: Temporal has no not-yet-started executions or second parents, so pending, skipped, linked and origin are expressed with search attributes GET /workflows can filter on, keeping NFR-7's existing fields and Temporal statuses underneath.

technology_choices.choice: Computed in the backend: each stage and onboarding upserts WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings search attributes as its state changes and clears WaitingForUser when it closes; the TaskWorkflow aggregates its children's states, signalled by them, into its own attributes; for closed flows the listing clears UnresolvedFindings when the existing findings acceptance record exists for the delivery run; GET /workflows returns both as new fields. Executions started before this change carry neither attribute and are listed without highlight or marker (the fields are null for them)
technology_choices.rationale: User's choice to compute the highlight in the backend; search attributes let the listing show it without querying every child, the acceptance record already holds acceptances given after a flow closed (FR-142, FR-143), closed flows are never waiting (FR-110), and the listing only gains fields (NFR-7). User chose not to backfill old-shape flows: they are only listed.

technology_choices.choice: A RequirementsReviewWorkflow per task or onboarding on the main queue, created pending by the TaskWorkflow and started on finalize. It runs every round of the review in one execution, calling the LLM through the existing adapters with the requirements_review model settings entry (shared by tasks and onboardings). From the second round on it is given the requirements diff plus the contradiction questions and answers. It talks to the interview stage by Temporal signals and closes as passed, continued anyway or skipped. A round whose LLM activity fails after Temporal's retries is marked failed with the error; the user retries it through a retry action like a failed turn, or forces past it; force cancels a running round.
technology_choices.rationale: FR-144 to FR-158 and FR-153: a child flow of its own shown on the Flows page, with unlimited rounds that wait on the user's answers. The diff tells the reviewer what changed and the answers tell it how the user meant to resolve each contradiction (FR-147). One settings entry keeps Settings simple (FR-148). The user chose that a failed review round can be retried like a failed turn or forced past, and that force writes the document at once even while a round runs.

technology_choices.choice: Cancelled on deploy: an idempotent startup step of the API cancels every running top-level OnboardingWorkflow (no parent task flow) with its children; they stay listed as cancelled in the All view and must be started again.
technology_choices.rationale: User's choice; avoids keeping the onboarding ID field and the old onboarding flow shape alive alongside the task flow shape (FR-159, FR-164).
